ety.text: Borrowed from Latin as. Doublet of ace.
Shortening of as hell or as fuck or similar.

senses.d: To such an extent or degree; to the same extent or degree.
ex: She regards her kids as (being) holy as saints.
You’re not as tall as I am, but you are definitely as happy as can be.

senses.d: Considered to be, in relation to something else; in the relation (specified).
For example; for instance. (Compare such as.)
ex: Likewise many other indulgences were by virtue hereof granted; as, to have a portatile altar, to receive the Sacrament privately; […]
First; original; indigenous; primitive; native; as, the aboriginal tribes of America.

senses.d: In the (same) way or manner that; to the (same) degree that.
ex: Do as I say!
I'm under a lot of pressure, as you know.

senses.d: Used after so or as to introduce a comparison.
ex: She's twice as strong as I was two years ago.
It's not so complicated as I expected.

senses.d: Used to introduce a result: with the result that it is; as to.

ex: (As) much as I respect your viewpoint, I can’t agree.
(As) bravely as they fought, they soon lost the battle.

senses.d: At the same instant or moment that: when.
ex: As I came in, she fled.

senses.d: At the same time that, during the same time when: while.
ex: He sleeps as the rain falls.

senses.d: Varying through time in the same proportion that.
ex: As my fear grew, so did my legs become heavy.
As she grew older, she grew wiser.

senses.d: Being that, considering that, because, since.
ex: As it’s too late, I quit.
(As) tired as he was, I decided not to disturb him.

senses.d: Introducing a comparison with a hypothetical state (+ subjunctive, or with the verb elided): as though, as if.
ex: And sodenly there cam a sounde from heven as it had bene the commynge off a myghty wynde […]

Oft haue I ſeene the haughty Cardinall,
 More like a Souldier then a man o' th' Church,
 As ſtout and proud as he were Lord of all […]

senses.d: used before a preposition to clarify that the prepositional phrase restricts the meaning of the sentence; specifically.
ex: The case is dismissed as between Jones and Smith.
The case is dismissed as against Smith.

senses.d: Introducing a basis of comparison, with an object in the objective case.
ex: You are not as tall as my sister.
They are big as houses.
What is your opinion as a parent?
As your big sis, I worry about your life too.
I bought you a new toy as a special treat.

senses.d: Any of several coins of Rome, coined in bronze or later copper; or the equivalent value.
Used to intensify an adjective; very much; extremely.
ex: sweet as

It also appears in other positions in the sentence: his big as car could hardly fit.
It's pretty scratched, and dented as.
